recipes.name: Overnight Blueberry French Toast
ingredients_raw: 12 slices day-old bread, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 (8 ounce) packages cream cheese, cut into 1 inch cubes

steps.text: Prepare casserole: Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Arrange 1/2 of the bread cubes in the dish and top with cream cheese cubes.
Sprinkle blueberries over the cream cheese, then top with remaining bread cubes.
Whisk eggs, milk, vanilla extract, and syrup together in a large bowl until well-combined; pour over the bread cubes. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Remove casserole from the refrigerator about 30 minutes before baking. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bake casserole in the preheated oven, covered, for 30 minutes. Uncover, and continue baking until center is firm and surface is lightly browned, about 25 to 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, prepare blueberry sauce: Mix sugar, water, and cornstarch together in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil and cook, stirring constantly, 3 to 4 minutes. Stir in blueberries, reduce heat to low, and simmer until all the blueberries burst, about 10 minutes. Stir in butter.
Serve portions of casserole on plates and pour warm syrup over top.

raw_recipe.headline: Overnight Blueberry French Toast
raw_recipe.description: This make-ahead blueberry French toast casserole is easy to prep the night before and bake in the morning for a pleasing holiday breakfast or brunch.

review.reviewBody: YUM! I made this for Christmas morning for my inlaws. It turned out great. I did take a lot of the suggestions and modified this recipe. Here's what I did: Used Italian bread from the bakery (French bread seemed like too much crust). I also whipped 1 1/2 bricks cream cheese w/ 1/4 cup confectioners sugar and spread it over the cubed bread. I used frozen blueberries (thawed) and only 10 eggs. I also made sure to press the bread down so that everything got french toast consistancy. The syrup is delicious!! I made 1.5 times and poured 2/3 of it over the dish and the other 1/3 was put on the table for those who wanted a little bit more. Overall, this is a great recipe!! Will be sure to make at my next brunch. Thank you!

Delicious and beautiful, and perfect just as written. I used a good quality Italian bread, and chose to serve the blueberry sauce on the side. My out of town guests, both of whom are professional chefs, loved this so much they asked for the recipe. Gooey, creamy and crunchy all at the same time, depending on what forkful hits your mouth! Any leftover sauce (I made a double recipe of it) would be great on waffles, pancakes, pound cake or ice cream. We all enjoyed this very much!

I've made this for every Christmas breakfast for 20yrs. I've made alterations over the years but the only one I've stuck with is how I incorporate the cream cheese. None of us liked biting into a glommy chunk of cr. cheese! So, I put half the bread in the pan, sprinkle the blueberries in and then the rest of the bread. After bringing the cr. cheese to room temp I beat it in my stand mixer with the whisk attachment. When it is smooth and soft, I whisk in the eggs a couple at a time, making sure all are well incorporated before adding more. After all the eggs are mixed in, I whisk in the milk, vanilla extract and maple syrup. Then I pour this mixture over the bread and blueberries. Continue with the overnight and baking instructions as they are listed here.

Great recipe, followed to the letter first time and the 2nd time I tried freezing and grating the cream cheese to avoid huge gobs of uncooked cream cheese in the dish- that worked better BUT the 3rd time I made this, I spread the cream cheese on the pieces of bread before cutting into smaller pieces- little messy but more effective and better tasting. I also added vanilla to eggs and added nutmeg and cinnamon to the first and last layer of bread cubes.

Amazing! Used 12 slices of french bread. Whipped 2 packs of softened cream cheese, 1/2 cup milk, 1 T vanilla and 1/3 cup sugar together, spread on the bread, then cubed. 10 eggs instead of 12. So, 6 slices, then cream cheese, 1-2 cups blueberries, six more slices, then egg/milk mixture. Pressed down mixture to ensure absorption. Set out for a half hour, cooked as directed. It was a huge hit!

Yummy taste but needed to firm up bottom layer - next time will bake longer-only made 1/2 recipe so surprised. However this was my second time making this and I followed other reviews and it was very improved! Spreading cream cheese mixed with powdered sugar helped. Less cream cheese and eggs were a big help. I used only 3/4 pkg cream cheese and 5 eggs for half a recipe.

This is a family favorite. Like many others, I blend the cream cheese with some confectioners sugar and pipe it across the center. I’ve continued to make the full 2 pkg batch, but reserve about 1/3 of it to put on during baking, just after pulling the cover for the last 25-30m session. Even my picky eaters gobble this up.

This would be a total breakfast indulgence for me the way it’s written, so I did try to lighten it a bit by using Egg Beaters for the eggs, Truvia for the sugar, and reduced fat cream cheese. And that worked out great with no sacrifice to flavor. The video shows pressing down on the bread cubes before moving to the fridge, and that’s a great idea. That will help moisten ALL of the bread, not just the bottom. Only thing I would change is cutting both the bread and the cream cheese into a little smaller cubes next time. I lucked out and bought some of the sweetest blueberries I’ve ever had which made an amazing sauce. What a treat, simply outstanding, and definitely would make again.

This is a fabulous recipe as written, I bet, but I had to make a lot of adjustments, based on what I had on hand this first time I am following this recipe, while also reading from the reviews. I absolutely love how highly adaptable this recipe is, though. You can make it from frozen waffles, you can make it in the morning to have breakfast for dinner, plus you can easily change up the flavor profile to other fruits, even!

I will make so many versions of this going forward, most definitely. Thank you dearly for posting this!

You must try it with lemon extract added with the vanilla.

My only substitution was I used frozen blueberries instead of fresh. I’m thinking this is why mine took 1 hour and 25 minutes to cook, as oppose to the recipe’s recommended 1 hour. I used a brioche bread. I did have an addition of the zest of 1 lemon and the juice of 1/2 a lemon in the sauce, HOWEVER I did make the sauce as directed in the recipe AND I tried it before making those additions. It was VERY sweet and did need the acid to brighten it up. I served my sauce on the side along with homemade whipped cream and it was FANTABULOUS!

I've made this twice. We love it. The second time I was out of lemon. It was very flat. I bought a lemon and added zest and juice and it is super now. I do have to make extra blueberry syrup/sauce. I've made it with good quality store-bought white sandwich bread and with home-made whole wheat sourdough. It's good with either, though the cream cheese was more noticable with white bread. I may have used too much bread in the sourdough one. I will definitely keep making it. Thanks for the recipe.
I make this way, and I do a variation with bacon, bourbon and maple. Both are frequent requests!

My family loves this! We have been making it for the past several years. It is our go-to for Thanksgiving morning and New Years Day, and it is often a birthday-breakfast request. Rather than cutting the cream cheese, I spread it on slices of the bread before cubing the bread. I do find it typically takes longer to cook in my oven than the recipe suggests (closer to 1:20), but it's always a hit!
I use challah bread. Soooo good

Won't make this again. The crispy top bread was great, but the very soggy body of the dish was unappetizing. The cream cheese didn't melt evenly throughout despite following the directions explicitly. It might be better to blend the cream cheese in with the egg mixture to ensure even distribution. But still, how to eliminate the soggy bottom?
This was unexpectedly delicious although next time I will bake longer because some of the egg did not cook, but this is easily rectified.
I used only half of the cream cheese and it was plenty! I also added slivered almonds to the top before baking and it was a great addition.
After cooking for 1 1/2 hour it was a wet mess. Maybe use less milk? Tasted okay - but I would not make it again.
Family Favorite!!!
